rules.title: Repeated connector pin functions differ
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: Pins with matching meaningful normalized functions on repeated connector symbols, or within one symbol, use different or missing net assignments. A complete source-matched project interface map can supply a return role when native function text is absent, generic Pin_N, or numeric-only; this can compare returns across different connector symbols. The same map can compare generic or numeric-only supply contacts across symbols only when their exact authored voltage_domain values match. Numeric function text can identify a comparable contact within an exact repeated symbol by itself, but does not establish an electrical role. Generic KiCad Pin_N labels remain unknown unless the source-matched map supplies a supported role. When every participating connector has a current source-matched peer_assignment_group, non-return and non-supply comparisons are partitioned by that group; return and supply role comparisons remain cross-group. Incomplete or stale group coverage retains the unscoped comparison.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Matching functions are only candidate evidence; the rule cannot decide whether nets must be common, bonded, or isolated.

Project-mapped return roles are used only from a complete interface entry whose catalog digest, component pin inventory, native pin functions, and net assignments match the current native netlist; role classification still does not require commonality.

Project-mapped supply roles are compared across symbols only when a complete source-matched interface map supplies the same exact voltage_domain text for both contacts. A matching role and domain prompt review; they do not prove that nets must be common or that independent, switched, ORed, or isolated sources are invalid.
A numeric function such as 7 is compared only as matching native function text within an exact repeated symbol; it does not mean ground, supply, or a required common connection.

A peer_assignment_group scopes which connector instances are compared; group membership does not require their nets to match, and distinct groups do not assert that their nets must remain separate. A review basis is required, and incomplete or stale group evidence does not suppress the broad comparison.
Without a source-matched interface role, absent functions and generic Pin_N placeholders do not establish matching roles; exact-symbol peer assignment rules handle those contacts at lower confidence.

Automatic candidates are numeric J/P/X/CN references and symbols in standard Connector libraries except Connector:TestPoint; an exact project-reviewed interface reference can additionally classify a custom symbol. Other aliases and library families can evade candidate discovery.
References listed as DNP by the native netlist are excluded from population-dependent comparisons.

rules.title: Repeated connector symbol pin has an outlier assignment
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: Among fitted connector instances using the exact same library symbol, the same pin number is unconnected on an outlier peer or differs from a unique most-common schematic net assignment shared by at least two instances; at least one peer pin lacks a meaningful function because its metadata is absent or a generic Pin_N placeholder. When every participating connector has current source-matched peer_assignment_group evidence, comparisons are partitioned within each group; incomplete or stale group coverage retains the unscoped comparison.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Identical symbol and pin number identify comparable contacts but do not establish a required common net; per-port isolation, optional contacts, and unused pins can be intentional.
A tied most-common assignment does not identify an outlier and is delegated to connector.peer_pin_assignment_divergence.

A peer_assignment_group identifies comparison scope only; it does not establish a required common net. Distinct groups are excluded from comparison only while all participating connector group reviews are current and complete.

Automatic candidates are numeric J/P/X/CN references and symbols in standard Connector libraries except Connector:TestPoint; an exact project-reviewed interface reference can additionally classify a custom symbol. Other aliases and library families can evade candidate discovery. Missing symbol identity or pin-number inventory can evade comparison.
The check is limited to cases where at least one peer has absent or generic Pin_N function metadata and does not establish PCB copper connectivity or off-board wiring.
DNP connector instances are excluded, and the result remains a review hint subject to project rule overrides or an exact ignore.

rules.title: Generic peer connector pin assignments differ
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: Among fitted connector instances using the exact same library symbol, the same pin number is assigned to different schematic nets, all compared contacts are assigned, fewer than two peers have meaningful pin-function metadata (absent or generic Pin_N labels are unknown), and no unique most-common assignment exists. This lower-confidence prompt covers two-peer or tied groups while leaving uniquely-majoritized outliers to the outlier rule. When every participating connector has current source-matched peer_assignment_group evidence, comparisons are partitioned within each group; incomplete or stale group coverage retains the unscoped comparison.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Identical symbol and pin number do not establish that contacts should share a net; separate ports, isolated domains, and intentional per-port assignments can all be valid.
A unique most-common assignment is handled by connector.peer_pin_assignment_outlier; a lower-confidence divergence prompt is retained only when the assignments have no unique mode.

A peer_assignment_group identifies comparison scope only; it does not establish a required common net. Distinct groups are excluded from comparison only while all participating connector group reviews are current and complete.

Automatic candidates are numeric J/P/X/CN references and symbols in standard Connector libraries except Connector:TestPoint; an exact project-reviewed interface reference can additionally classify a custom symbol. Other aliases and library families can evade candidate discovery. Unknown pin roles must be reviewed against an approved interface pinout before any contract is authored.
Unassigned contacts are left to the existing peer-outlier and named-pin rules; groups with complete meaningful pin-function roles remain with connector.repeated_pin_function.
DNP connector instances are excluded, and the result does not establish PCB copper connectivity or off-board wiring.

rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist

supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The bounded function aliases can miss vendor-specific control names and do not establish required bias, polarity, startup state, or whether a local resistor is needed.

Only direct fitted conventional two-terminal resistor assignments to recognized rail names or pin functions are recognized. DNP resistors, series paths, resistor arrays, jumpers, active bias circuits, custom rail names, and unusual component identities can produce a review prompt.
Internal pulls, off-board bias, connected drivers, firmware behavior, resistor adequacy, and PCB copper continuity are not modeled; DNP control components are excluded.

rules.title: Named I2C bus lacks visible local pull-up path
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: A component with distinct assigned SDA and SCL nets has either line without a visible 1 kΩ through 100 kΩ path to a named positive rail. A path is one conventional fitted resistor or an unbranched series chain of fitted conventional resistors, with each resistor and the total nominal resistance in range; every intermediate net must contain exactly the two recognized resistor pins.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Internal device pull-ups and off-board pull-ups are invisible in this netlist and can produce valid review findings.
Branched or otherwise ambiguous resistor junctions are not followed. The check does not analyze resistor placement, tolerance, bus capacitance, voltage compatibility, or timing.

A resistor-array hint is resolved only by an exact project-authored I2C requirement whose SDA and SCL checks pass against this native netlist; missing, pending, not-applicable, mismatched, or failing requirements leave the review open.

rules.title: I2C pull-up equivalent resistance is below the review band
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For a recognized assigned SDA/SCL bus, fitted conventional R-reference resistors from 1 kΩ through 100 kΩ are grouped into direct or unbranched series paths with total nominal resistance in the same range. Paths to one named positive rail are combined in parallel; a line is reported when its nominal equivalent resistance is below 1 kΩ.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The 1 kΩ boundary is a broad review threshold, not a universal electrical requirement; project-specific requirements and rule modes remain authoritative.
Only directly connected or unbranched series paths of discrete resistors are recognized; arrays, branched paths, multiple pull-up rails, internal pull-ups, and remote pull-ups are not calculated.

This heuristic uses nominal resistance only and does not establish resistor tolerance, sink-current margin, bus voltage compatibility, capacitance, rise time, or timing. A separate project-authored electrical-window check can optionally apply a maximum per-resistor tolerance bound, but does not verify its cited source or scope.

rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist

Emit one review candidate when the combined SDA/SCL paths use more than one distinct normalized positive-rail family.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Rail families come from a narrow net-name or pin-function allowlist. Custom positive rail names without a recognized power-pin function are not included.

Different families are a review cue, not proof of incompatible voltages. The check does not resolve rail values, device input limits, level shifting, rail sequencing, external pull-ups, resistor arrays, or active pull-up circuits.
Only fitted conventional resistor paths with each resistor and total path in the 1 kΩ–100 kΩ detection range are followed; this is not a universal I2C resistor requirement.

rules.title: Active-low SPI chip-select input has no visible local pull-up
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: A non-DNP pin with an explicitly active-low chip-select function and native input/input_low electrical type has one assigned non-return net, while no fitted conventional resistor path from that net to a recognized positive rail has a per-resistor and total nominal value between 1 kΩ and 100 kΩ. A missing visible path can be valid when the device has an internal bias, the controller guarantees the idle state, or bias is supplied off-board; no firmware or runtime state is inspected.

Only recognized positive rail names or pin functions count, and only direct or unbranched conventional two-terminal resistor chains are traced. Resistor arrays, jumpers, active bias circuits, and uncommon rail labels are outside the predicate.
The 1 kΩ–100 kΩ interval is a broad review-detection window, not a recommended value or proof of valid logic thresholds, reset sequencing, device selection, or signal integrity.

rules.title: USB-C CC pin is unassigned
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: A symbol pin function CC1 or CC2 is absent from every exported net.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The rule checks assignment only; it does not determine host/device role or the required CC resistor network.
Unusual library naming and off-board CC circuitry are outside the evidence.

rules.title: Likely USB-C connector has no reviewed port role
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including connector references, exported CC1/CC2 pin functions, assignments, and the source-hashed project electrical contract
rules.predicate: For a non-DNP connector candidate whose exported symbol pin functions include both CC1 and CC2, report when its component reference is absent from the project-authored USB-C port map or no USB-C port role map is configured.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Only exact CC1 and CC2 pin-function names are recognized. Automatic connector identities are numeric J/P/X/CN references and standard Connector library symbols; an exact project-reviewed interface reference can include a custom symbol.

A symbol using both pin-function names may not be a USB-C port. The finding asks for review and does not infer source, sink, dual-role, Rp/Rd, controller, VBUS, ground, protection, or USB compliance requirements.
A connector listed in the authored USB-C map is considered covered even if its pin assignments are wrong; the electrical contract reports those separate mismatches. DNP connectors are excluded.
Schematic pin assignments do not establish controller configuration, component conduction, PCB copper continuity, off-board behavior, or physical connector wiring.

rules.title: Project-mapped USB data path differs from PHY-specific topology
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For a project-authored connector-to-PHY interface, exact connector and PHY symbol/footprint identities, endpoint pin inventory and net assignments, and the declared direct path or fitted series-resistor identity, value range, and two-net topology must match. A common_net or separate_nets reference policy checks the mapped endpoint reference pins; a bonded policy additionally requires one exact passive two-pin component identity, value, footprint, and side-pin net assignment between the two declared reference nets.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The project must author the PHY-specific topology and cite its engineering basis; this rule does not infer that every USB PHY needs or forbids an external resistor.

Only direct paths and one mapped conventional two-terminal resistor per data line are modeled. Additional series components, arrays, USB-C role behavior, USB 3.x lanes, signal integrity, PCB placement, and copper continuity need separate requirements or evidence.
A passing schematic netlist comparison does not validate the selected resistor range against a datasheet or prove electrical or manufacturing suitability.

A mapped reference bond checks native schematic symbol, footprint, value, DNP state, passive pin types, and net assignments; it does not prove component conduction, board copper continuity, or off-board grounding.

rules.title: Recognized CAN line pin is unassigned
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: A pin function normalizing to CANH, CAN_HIGH, CANL, or CAN_LOW is absent from every exported net.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Pin-name aliases vary between vendors; this rule does not identify every transceiver or connector pair.
It does not infer whether a local CAN line is required or prove off-board continuity.

rules.title: Named CAN pair lacks visible direct termination
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: A component exposing distinct assigned CANH and CANL nets has no fitted direct two-terminal resistor from 108 Ω through 132 Ω across those nets.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: External and split termination are not represented as a direct local resistor and can produce valid review findings.
The rule does not evaluate bus topology, placement, resistor power, edge quality, or physical impedance.

rules.title: CAN peers sharing one line use different complementary nets
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For fitted source components with exactly one recognized CANH and one CANL pin function, both uniquely assigned to distinct native nets, emit a REVIEW finding when two or more complete pairs share one exact net on either side but use multiple exact nets on the other side.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The recognized function aliases are bounded to CANH/CAN_HIGH and CANL/CAN_LOW; vendor-specific labels, incomplete pairs, multi-pin role groups, ambiguous assignments, same-net pairs, and DNP parts are skipped.

Shared assignment on one side does not prove that components belong to one bus or that both sides must be common. Intentional split domains, gateways, isolated segments, and special topologies need project review or an explicit contract.
The rule checks schematic net assignments only. It does not establish termination, transceiver behavior, off-board wiring, PCB copper continuity, or physical connectivity.

rules.title: Complementary signal pair has incomplete net assignment
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: Within one symbol, a recognized built-in pair or project-authored pin-function alias bound to an exact KiCad symbol identity is missing a counterpart function, has multiple pins on one side, lacks a unique net assignment, or places both functions on one schematic net.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Built-in pin-function aliases are bounded to the documented names. Project-authored aliases are opt-in, scoped to an exact native KiCad symbol identity, and require a review basis; a stale symbol or function mapping blocks lint until refreshed.
Lane-indexed USB-C TX1/TX2 and RX1/RX2 pairs are outside this single-pair-per-role heuristic.

The rule does not infer a project requirement, validate signal polarity, prove off-board continuity, or establish physical pair routing; aliases describe project review intent, not electrical approval.
Fitted-symbol assignments are reviewed. DNP symbols are skipped; an intentionally unused fitted pair or deliberate same-net test mode needs an exact project-owned ignore or another reviewed decision.

rules.title: Named complementary nets lack a reviewed differential-pair requirement
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, compared with the optional project-owned differential-pair rule map
rules.predicate: Two populated source nets match one of the explicit complementary suffix pairs _P/_N, _DP/_DM, _TXP/_TXN, _RXP/_RXN, _H/_L, +/-, DP/DM, P/N, or H/L and are absent from the project-authored differential-pair rule map.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: This is a net-name review hint. It does not prove that the nets form a physical differential pair, inspect PCB geometry, or supply an acceptable width, gap, skew, or uncoupled-length limit.
Naming conventions can produce false positives or miss vendor-specific and unnamed pairs; an explicit project map or per-project review decision controls the finding.
An exact mapped pair suppresses this missing-requirement prompt; native-rule coverage and source-bound PCB DRC remain separate checks.

rules.title: Reviewed interface pin has no protection disposition
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-reviewed connector pin map and KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: A connector pin bound by the project interface catalog has no exact protection channel map or reasoned not-required disposition, except pins explicitly covered by the existing USB-C electrical contract.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: A missing disposition is a review prompt only; the rule does not infer that protection is required from a connector, protocol, signal name, or symbol reference.
The check only sees connector pins mapped by the project interface catalog and cannot discover unlisted interfaces or prove integrated protection from a component name.

rules.title: Mapped external protection differs from the source netlist
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored protection channel and component pin-net map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native XML netlist evidence
rules.predicate: A required interface protector is absent, DNP, has a different symbol or footprint, has an incomplete pin disposition, or its declared connector, signal, or reference pins use different native net assignments.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The project datasheet map supplies device purpose and internal topology; the netlist only verifies exact component identity and pin-to-net assignments.
This does not evaluate clamp voltage, pulse rating, capacitance, package suitability, placement, return-via geometry, or protection effectiveness.

rules.title: Return-like nets have a numbered common stem
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: At least two distinct net names have the same recognized return-like stem and different numeric suffixes. A recognized ground stem may use a one-letter suffix such as GNDA before an optional numeric suffix.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Suffix similarity is only a review clue; separate numbered returns can be intentional isolation domains.
Only documented return-like stems and numeric suffix patterns are recognized.

rules.title: Return-like net labels lack explicit pin roles
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: At least two distinct populated net names contain a recognized return token, are not already included in a numbered-return group, and have no attached exported symbol pin function that identifies a return. Recognized ground names include one-letter suffixes such as GNDA and GNDD.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Net-label text does not establish that domains must be connected, bonded, or isolated; the finding only prompts review.

Only documented return tokens and native pin-function text are recognized; a one-letter suffix extends GND only (for example GNDA or GNDD). Longer labels such as GNDAUDIO are not matched. Unrelated labels, missing symbol metadata, or an attached pin with a recognized return function can suppress this candidate.
The rule does not inspect PCB copper, off-board wiring, connector datasheets, or physical continuity.

rules.title: Positive supply nets have a numbered common stem
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: At least two distinct populated or unpopulated net names use either an explicitly delimited numeric suffix or a bounded P/CH/RAIL numeric prefix and the same recognized positive supply stem, such as +5V_1 and 5V-2 or CH2_VDD and CH3_VDD.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Name similarity only prompts review; sibling supply nets may be intentionally isolated or represent independent sources, and this rule never asserts that they should be joined.

Only a bounded list of positive-supply stems is recognized. Numeric suffixes require an explicit separator; numeric prefixes are limited to P, CH, and RAIL namespaces followed by an allowlisted supply stem. Unrecognized aliases and compact forms remain outside this rule.
The rule does not inspect source capability, voltage compatibility, fitted power-path devices, PCB copper, off-board wiring, or physical continuity.

rules.title: Native-unconnected pin has wire endpoint on its segment
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 schematic geometry joined to the matching native netlist's unconnected-pin set
rules.predicate: For a pin marked unconnected by the native netlist, a wire endpoint lies within 0.001 mm of its transformed tip-to-body segment and more than 0.001 mm from the pin tip.
limitations: Only schematic format 20231120, project-local hierarchical sheets with exact per-instance reference mappings, single-unit single-conversion symbols, orthogonal rotations, and x/y mirrors are supported; partial and unsupported coverage is reported.
This review hint localizes a geometric candidate and does not prove intent, copper connectivity, or electrical correctness.
The check only runs when a project explicitly sets this rule to review or block; its catalog default is off.

rules.title: Native-unconnected pin tip touches a wire interior
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 schematic geometry joined to the matching native netlist's unconnected-pin set
rules.predicate: For a pin marked unconnected by the native netlist, the transformed pin tip lies within 0.001 mm of the strict interior of a wire segment.
limitations: Only schematic format 20231120, project-local hierarchical sheets with exact per-instance reference mappings, embedded single-unit and single-conversion symbols, orthogonal rotations, and x/y mirrors are supported; partial and unsupported coverage is reported.
Native ERC already reports the unconnected pin and may report a separate wire endpoint; this heuristic localizes a wire that crosses the pin tip but does not prove intent or electrical correctness.
The check only runs when a project explicitly sets this rule to review or block; its catalog default is off. It never inserts a junction or edits schematic geometry.

rules.title: Native-unconnected pin has a nearby wire endpoint
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 schematic geometry joined to the matching native netlist's unconnected-pin set
rules.predicate: For a pin marked unconnected by the native netlist and without an explicit no-connect marker, report each wire endpoint more than 0.001 mm and no more than 0.5 mm from its transformed tip, except endpoints already on the pin segment.
limitations: Only schematic format 20231120, project-local hierarchical sheets with exact per-instance reference mappings, embedded single-unit and single-conversion symbols, orthogonal rotations, and x/y mirrors are supported; partial and unsupported coverage is reported.
Native ERC already reports the open pin and may report an unconnected wire endpoint; this heuristic improves localization and does not establish author intent, electrical connectivity, or a repair.

The fixed 0.5 mm search radius can include an unrelated nearby endpoint. The check only runs when a project explicitly sets the rule to review or block; its catalog default is off. It never changes schematic geometry.

rules.title: Schematic label narrowly misses a wire endpoint
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 schematic label and wire geometry, with native ERC used to confirm the synthetic fault and control
rules.predicate: For a supported local, global, or hierarchical label whose anchor is farther than 0.001 mm from every wire segment and pin tip, report each distinct wire endpoint more than 0.001 mm and no more than 1.27 mm away.
limitations: Only schematic format 20231120, project-local hierarchical sheets with exact per-instance reference mappings, and labels with a unique UUID and valid anchor are supported. Pin-tip exclusion uses symbol geometry the parser supports; unsupported symbols make coverage partial.
This is review-localization only. Native ERC already reports a dangling label in the validated fault; nearby geometry does not establish author intent or prove connectivity.

The fixed 1.27 mm search radius can produce unrelated nearby endpoint candidates and may not match a project's drawing grid. It does not diagnose junction semantics, hierarchical net connectivity, or copper connectivity.
The check only runs when a project explicitly sets this rule to review or block; its catalog default is off. It never moves labels or edits schematic geometry.

rules.title: Orthogonal wire interiors cross without a junction marker
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 hierarchical schematic geometry with exact per-instance references and matching native netlist evidence required by design lint
rules.predicate: Report distinct wire UUIDs whose axis-aligned segment interiors intersect at right angles within 0.001 mm and whose intersection has no junction marker within 0.001 mm.
limitations: Only schematic format 20231120 and project-local hierarchical sheets with exact per-instance reference mappings are supported; unsupported symbol geometry still makes the overall geometry scan partial.
An intentional unconnected crossing is valid and produces the same review candidate as a forgotten junction. This rule cannot infer intended connectivity from drawing geometry or net names.
Only orthogonal wire segment interiors are checked. Endpoint/T contacts, collinear overlap, diagonal segments, native electrical connectivity, and PCB copper are outside this predicate.
This rule is review-only by default and may be configured or exactly ignored per project; it never inserts junctions or edits schematic geometry.

rules.title: T-shaped wire contact lacks a junction marker
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 hierarchical schematic geometry with exact per-instance references and matching native netlist evidence required by design lint
rules.predicate: Report a wire endpoint within 0.001 mm of the strict interior of a different wire segment when no junction marker is within 0.001 mm.
limitations: Only schematic format 20231120 and project-local hierarchical sheets with exact per-instance reference mappings are supported; unsupported symbol geometry still makes the overall geometry scan partial.
A T-shaped drawing without a marker may represent an intentionally separate branch. Geometry suggests a likely connection but cannot establish project intent.

The rule does not inspect the exported netlist for a pin-level relationship, decide whether the branch must connect, or modify the schematic. It is review-only by default and can be overridden or exactly ignored per project.

rules.title: Free-text insertion anchors coincide
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 hierarchical schematic geometry joined to the matching native netlist evidence by design lint
rules.predicate: Report pairs of top-level free-text objects with non-empty content and unique UUIDs whose source insertion anchors are within 0.001 mm.
limitations: This compares insertion anchors only; it does not calculate rendered glyph bounds, text justification, font metrics, or actual visual overlap.
Coincident anchors may be intentional or may still render apart due to justification. The result is a review prompt, not an asserted drawing defect or electrical finding.
Only top-level free-text objects are included. Symbol properties, labels, text boxes, fields, and rendered-sheet imagery are outside this predicate.
The rule is off by default, can be enabled per project for review, and never moves or edits text.

rules.title: Distinct free-text envelopes overlap
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 schematic text geometry using standard-stroke glyph metrics measured from the digest-pinned native SVG exporter
rules.predicate: Report distinct top-level free-text objects whose conservative standard-font glyph envelopes intersect by at least 0.05 mm2 after a 0.08 mm per-edge guard; pairs with coincident anchors are handled by schematic.coincident_text_anchors.
limitations: Only top-level free text using the standard KiCad stroke font, 95 printable ASCII glyphs and measured U+00B0, U+00B1, U+00B5, U+00D7, U+03A9, and U+2014 glyphs, positive explicit font sizes, horizontal text, and centered/left/right justification is measured. Plain KiCad escaped line breaks are supported. Custom faces, bold or italic text, custom thickness, markup, other characters, unsupported justifications, rotations, and other drawing object types produce partial geometry coverage. KiCad serialized \n and \r line-break escapes are detected before metric lookup.

Axis-aligned glyph envelopes can intersect even when the individual stroke paths do not. Native SVG fault/control evidence validates the tested pair but does not eliminate false positives on other text shapes or layouts.

This is a graphical review hint only; it does not infer electrical intent, replace native ERC, or move/edit text. The rule is off by default and supports project review, block, off, and exact-ignore dispositions.

rules.title: Electrical wire crosses a free-text envelope
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 schematic geometry with standard-stroke glyph metrics measured from the digest-pinned native SVG exporter
rules.predicate: Report top-level free-text glyph envelopes crossed by a native wire centerline for at least 0.2 mm after a 0.12 mm per-edge guard.
limitations: Only top-level free text using the standard KiCad stroke font, 95 printable ASCII glyphs and measured U+00B0, U+00B1, U+00B5, U+00D7, U+03A9, and U+2014 glyphs, positive explicit font sizes, horizontal text, and centered/left/right justification is measured. Plain KiCad escaped line breaks are supported. Custom faces, bold or italic text, custom thickness, markup, other characters, unsupported justifications, rotations, and other drawing object types produce partial geometry coverage. KiCad serialized \n and \r line-break escapes are detected before metric lookup.

A guarded axis-aligned text envelope can intersect a wire even when individual glyph strokes do not. Native SVG fault/control evidence validates the tested crossing only; intentional annotation-over-wire layouts remain possible.

The rule examines native wire segments only, not buses, labels, symbol fields, pin names or numbers, symbol graphics, or PCB geometry. It is a graphical review hint, not an electrical finding or connectivity change. It is off by default and supports project review, block, off, and exact-ignore dispositions.

rules.title: Free text overlaps a symbol-body envelope
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 text glyph metrics and supported embedded symbol graphics
rules.predicate: Report top-level, supported free-text glyph envelopes overlapping a supported symbol-body envelope by at least 0.1 mm2 after a 0.1 mm text-edge guard and 0.15 mm symbol-body guard.
limitations: Only top-level free text using the standard KiCad stroke font, 95 printable ASCII glyphs and measured U+00B0, U+00B1, U+00B5, U+00D7, U+03A9, and U+2014 glyphs, positive explicit font sizes, horizontal text, and centered/left/right justification is measured. Plain KiCad escaped line breaks are supported. Unsupported text styles, other characters, unsupported justifications, or rotations leave geometry coverage partial. KiCad serialized \n and \r line-break escapes are detected before metric lookup.

Both text and symbol geometry use axis-aligned envelopes. Disjoint or non-rectangular symbol primitives and gaps between glyph strokes can produce candidates; intentional annotations over symbols remain possible.
Labels, symbol fields, pin names, sheet text, and other text objects are outside this rule. It is a graphical review hint, off by default, and does not establish connectivity or design intent.

rules.title: Electrical wire crosses a symbol-body envelope
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 schematic wire geometry and supported embedded symbol graphics
rules.predicate: For supported single-unit, single-conversion symbols with rectangle, polyline, bezier, or circle graphics, report a native wire centerline that remains at least 0.2 mm inside the axis-aligned body envelope and overlaps it for at least 0.3 mm.
limitations: The envelope bounds supported embedded symbol graphics after orthogonal rotation and x/y mirroring. Bounding several disjoint or non-rectangular primitives can include empty space; valid connector contacts inside a symbol outline and other intentional wire crossings can be review candidates.

Arcs, text graphics, multi-unit or multi-conversion symbols, unsupported transforms, or unrecognized body primitives leave geometry coverage partial. The rule does not infer pin connectivity, intended isolation, or schematic electrical meaning.
This is a graphical review hint only. It is off by default and supports project review, block, off, and exact-ignore dispositions; it never edits the schematic or replaces native ERC.

rules.title: Strapped I2C address differs from the project map
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored responder and address-pin map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native netlist evidence
rules.predicate: For a mapped strapped responder with exact symbol, bus-pin, address-pin-function, and low/high-net evidence, the resolved 7-bit address differs from the project-declared address.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The rule checks only responders and address-pin bits explicitly mapped by the project; it does not infer device addresses from references, values, or part names.
A source-bound netlist cannot establish firmware-selected addresses, off-board devices, boot-time changes, or mux topology absent from the project map.
A mapped symbol function is library metadata; correctness of the part pinout and project-authored address basis still requires review.

rules.title: Mapped I2C responders share a static address on one segment
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored segment and responder map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native netlist evidence
rules.predicate: Two or more fitted, completely mapped responders on the same project-declared SDA/SCL segment resolve to the same 7-bit static address.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Same-address responders on different declared segments are allowed; correctness of mux isolation and completeness of the segment map remain project review responsibilities.
Dynamic, unresolved, DNP, unlisted, off-board, or firmware-addressed devices do not produce collision findings; unresolved and dynamic entries remain coverage gaps.
The rule identifies address conflicts, not bus electrical compatibility or successful communication.

rules.title: Likely I2C responder is missing from the project address map
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including exported symbol pin functions and net assignments
rules.predicate: For a component not marked DNP with a U or IC reference, at least one uniquely assigned SDA function pin and one uniquely assigned SCL function pin on distinct nets, report it when the project address map is absent or does not list that reference.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The reference-prefix filter is limited to U and IC; other designator conventions are not discovered.
Only exact SDA, I2C_SDA, SCL, and I2C_SCL symbol function spellings are recognized after punctuation normalization; incorrect or missing library metadata can evade the prompt.

A component with SDA and SCL functions may be a bridge, translator, or other part that does not need a static address. This is a review candidate and does not assert that every such device is an addressable responder.
A mapped responder is treated as covered even if its pins or identity mismatch; the project-map comparison reports those separate source mismatches.

rules.title: Likely UART endpoint is missing from the project peer map
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including exported pin functions, exact net assignments and names, fitted state, and the source-hashed project serial-peer contract
rules.predicate: Report an unmapped fitted TX/RX candidate through either bounded path: (1) exact exported TX/TXD and RX/RXD pin-function pairs on distinct uniquely assigned nets within one component; or (2) one fitted U/IC pin on each distinct uniquely assigned UART/USART-labeled TX/RX net, with both nets also assigned to at least one common fitted connector candidate, when the exact pin pair is absent from the project serial_peers map. The label path is skipped when the MCU pin already exports a recognized serial function.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The pin-function path recognizes only bounded TX/TXD and RX/RXD spellings. The net-label path recognizes only exact UART/USART labels with optional channel digits and TX/RX suffixes; bare TX/RX labels, arbitrary aliases, missing net labels, and differently named channels are outside the predicate.

The net-label path requires exactly one fitted U/IC pin per role and a common fitted connector candidate on both nets. Ambiguous assignments, multiple candidate MCU pins, mismatched labels, absent connector candidates, and non-unique assignments are excluded.

Names and exported pin functions are discovery clues, not proof of protocol or endpoint intent. Unused MCU alternate functions, other serial standards, incomplete documentation, or labels that do not reflect the intended circuit can produce or suppress prompts.

A serial-map endpoint suppresses only its exact TX/RX pin pair; the separate source-bound serial contract reports wrong identity, pin, or net mappings. A map does not prove board copper continuity or external wiring.

This heuristic does not establish that a peer, connection, shared ground, voltage domain, or UART requirement is intended. It does not discover missing power or reference pins; those require connector inventory and authored pinout coverage.

rules.title: Likely SPI participant is missing from the project device map
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including exported symbol pin functions, net assignments, and the source-hashed project electrical contract
rules.predicate: For a non-DNP U- or IC-prefixed component, report a likely SPI participant when at least one uniquely assigned clock function (SCK/SCLK), one uniquely assigned data function (MOSI/SDI/COPI or MISO/SDO/CIPO), and one recognized chip-select function (CS/CSN/NCS/NSS/SS/SSEL/CE0/CE1) are present, and the reference is absent from the project-authored SPI controller/device/bridge roster or no required roster is configured.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The reference-prefix filter is limited to U and IC; other designator conventions are not discovered.
Only the listed exact pin-function aliases are recognized after punctuation normalization and an optional SPI prefix; missing or different library metadata can evade the prompt.
A controller, translator, multi-protocol device, or intentionally unused SPI-capable IC can match. The result is a coverage prompt and never asserts that the component must join an SPI bus.
A reference in the authored roster is considered covered even if its signal pins are wrong; the SPI contract comparison reports those separate mismatches.
This schematic-netlist check does not prove PCB copper continuity, internal transfer behavior, signal timing, or firmware configuration.

rules.title: SPI peers use different voltage-named supply rails
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including complete native pin-type inventories, exact SPI pin functions, pin/net assignments, and an optional source-hashed digital-peer voltage contract
rules.predicate: For fitted U- or IC-prefixed parts with complete native pin-type inventories and exactly one assigned positive power_in rail per part, report a REVIEW prompt when an exact recognized SPI signal function joins an output-capable pin to an input-capable pin and the two rail labels each contain exactly one explicit positive voltage token with different parsed nominal values. Suppress only exact endpoint/net/symbol/footprint matches with complete authored LINT-061 output and input limits.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Voltage values are parsed from exactly one token in each native net name and are review clues only; they do not establish actual rail voltage, source validity, tolerance, logic thresholds, output guarantees, or incompatibility.

Only U/IC references, exact normalized SPI clock/data/select aliases, known native input/output/bidirectional/tri-state signal types, complete pin-type inventories, and one assigned power_in supply net are supported. Missing metadata, open-collector/open-emitter pins, multiple supplies, unconnected supplies, and unrecognized functions are skipped.
A direct SPI signal net between two receivers or two drivers is not reported because electrical direction is ambiguous. Bidirectional pairs are skipped when both orientations are plausible.
Return-like power-input pins are excluded by exact return-like function or net-name context; custom ground aliases may be treated as supplies or make the candidate inapplicable.

Connector exclusions use numeric J/P/X/CN references, standard Connector libraries, and exact project-reviewed interface references; custom unreviewed symbols can still be treated as internal loads.

An opaque custom capacitor symbol name is not counted as capacitor evidence. When the supply net is otherwise recognized by the existing IC decoupling rule, that separate rule may independently report missing recognizable capacitor evidence.

Only fitted, exactly inventoried two-terminal low-resistance resistors, inductors, ferrite beads, fuses, polyfuses, the exact Jumper:SolderJumper_2_Bridged identity with native pins 1/2 mapped to A/B, and the exact Jumper:SolderJumper_3_Bridged12 or Jumper:SolderJumper_3_Bridged123 identities with complete native pins 1/2/3 mapped to A/C/B count as bidirectional paths. Bridged12 joins only pins 1 and 2; Bridged123 joins all three. Open, DNP, other, or ambiguously mapped solder jumpers remain unsupported and may produce extra review prompts. Exact Device:D and Device:D_Schottky identities count only with one native A pin and one native K pin on distinct nets, and only in the source-to-load direction. Zener, TVS, custom diode, switch, regulator, semiconductor, and ambiguous-pin paths remain unsupported and may produce extra review prompts.

A fitted power_out pin counts as a source anchor even when a regulator, switch, or other device is not operational. The finding does not prove that a connection is required, that a component conducts, or that current direction, electrical ratings, PCB copper, off-board wiring, assembly state, or manufacturing are valid.

rules.title: Connector/capacitor-only net has no visible local DC anchor
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For each non-return net, emit a review candidate when every fitted assigned pin belongs to a recognized connector or supported capacitor symbol and the net contains at least one pin of each; DNP references are excluded, and any unknown or other fitted component pin suppresses the candidate.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: A connector can receive its DC level from an off-board host, and an IC can have internal bias; the candidate does not establish that a local bias is required or missing.

The rule checks only the native pins assigned to one schematic net. It does not trace a complete DC path, evaluate component states or values, identify an analog function, or prove PCB and off-board connectivity.
Capacitor recognition is limited to Device:C, Device:CP, and library symbol IDs containing Capacitor. Unknown capacitor aliases and symbol metadata are skipped or suppress a candidate.

Any additional fitted non-connector, non-capacitor pin suppresses the candidate, even when that component does not provide a DC reference; DNP pins are excluded. Connector identity uses the bounded automatic candidate set and exact project-reviewed interface references.
Return-like nets and pins with return-like function names are excluded. Custom return names, external circuitry, internal pulls, resistor arrays, and component-internal paths are not modeled.

rules.title: STM32 CubeMX pin map differs from the KiCad schematic
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist plus a project-local, SHA-256-bound STM32CubeMX IOC file
rules.predicate: A project-mapped package port pin is absent, has a different CubeMX Signal or checked GPIO_Label, maps to the wrong KiCad symbol pin, has a different schematic net, or belongs to a different MCU part/symbol; a bounded STM32 identity hint requests a map when no contract exists.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; each project native receipt verifies its exact catalogued KiCad version before netlist comparison
limitations: STM32 discovery uses only the literal STM32 token in component value or symbol ID and can miss other MCU families or nonstandard identities.
The project must author a complete package-pin inventory, map each signal pin to a symbol pin, and cite the reviewed pinout basis; the check cannot establish that the authored package map is correct.
The rule compares selected IOC Signal and GPIO_Label values. It does not compile firmware, validate silicon capabilities, prove PCB routing, or establish off-board behavior.

Only the bounded UTF-8 line syntax for CubeMX .Signal and .GPIO_Label assignments is parsed, including physical-pin alternate-function suffixes with hyphens or escaped spaces; duplicate fields, conflicting raw keys that normalize to one physical pin, and unsupported pin keys block comparison instead of being guessed.
